# ethereum-optimism/design-docs Weekly Report (Apr 5 - 11, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week, the repository focused on formalizing core protocol mechanics, specifically regarding gas models and sequencer metering. A major milestone was reached with the completion of the Sequencer-Defined Metering (SDM) design, alongside the introduction of a new proposal for "opgas" to refine fee rebates. Parallel to these architectural advancements, the team aggressively tackled technical debt, resolving several long-standing flaky tests and finalizing Service Level Agreement (SLA) updates for the Supernode. The week’s activity reflects a dual priority of stabilizing the current testing infrastructure while laying the groundwork for more sophisticated resource pricing within the OP Stack.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Protocol & Gas Economics
The project saw significant progress in defining how the Superchain handles resource metering and fee structures.
*   **Opgas Design Proposal:** An initial draft for the `opgas` design document was submitted ([#361](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/361)). This document synthesizes existing concepts regarding fee rebates and proposes a new gas model for Optimism, impacting both `protocol/opgas.md` and `protocol/sdm.md`.
*   **Sequencer-Defined Metering (SDM):** The design phase for SDM was officially concluded ([#360](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/360)). This comprehensive work included problem definition, implementation planning, and benchmarking for how sequencers manage throughput and metering.

### Infrastructure & Tooling
*   **Supernode SLA Updates:** Final updates for the `op-supernode` were merged, specifically addressing Full Outputs in the Denylist and the integration of the Denylist for `OptimisticOutput` ([#19180](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19180)).
*   **Template Enhancements:** A new PR was opened to improve contributor workflows by adding reminders regarding third-party service dependencies within project templates ([#373](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/pull/373)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues: Stability & Bug Fixes
The team successfully resolved several critical flaky tests that were impacting CI reliability:
*   **Sync & State Issues:** `TestTruncateDatabaseOnELResync` was fixed to resolve CrossSafe sync timeouts ([#19897](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19897)), and `TestExecutePayloadSuccess` was closed following a root cause analysis of asynchronous ExEx store population ([#19898](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19898)).
*   **P2P & Reorgs:** `TestReorgInvalidExecMsgs` was unskipped and closed ([#19712](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19712)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Reactive Runtime Configuration:** A significant new issue was opened ([#19981](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19981)) to address verifier nodes rejecting valid blocks during signer address rotations. The proposed solution involves a reactive reload mechanism or a grace period for key transitions.
*   **Persistent Test Flakiness:** Several tests remain under active investigation due to timing races and CI timeouts, notably `TestFlashblocksTransfer` ([#19934](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19934)), where block times are exceeding flashblock times, and `TestSuperchain` ([#19586](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/19586)), which is experiencing suspected panics during Sepolia fork tests.
*   **Interop Migration:** Work has begun to migrate `op-e2e` interop action tests to the `op-acceptance-tests` suite to streamline the testing architecture ([#18974](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/issues/18974)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week was characterized by deep technical troubleshooting between core contributors. Developers `wwared`, `maurelian`, and `sebastianst` were heavily involved in diagnosing complex race conditions within the flashblock and gap-fill testing logic. The transition of interop tests, noted by `inphi`, suggests an ongoing effort to reorganize responsibilities across different repositories within the Optimism ecosystem. The level of detail in the CI failure analyses indicates a highly diligent approach to maintaining the integrity of the protocol's codebase.
